CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right ankle injury from basketball.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son. Patient reports he went up for a shot when his son collided with him. Upon landing, patient twisted and rolled his ankle. He describes pain on the lateral (outside) aspect of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient reports difficulty walking and sensation of ankle instability. He denies feeling the ankle is solid or stable. Patient has recently returned to a regular workout routine and is concerned about disrupting his progress. He also mentions having volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain and instability in right ankle. Denies other acute complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Patient recently returned to exercising and working out regularly.

MEDICATIONS
None reported prior to this visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son (Sean, age 10) plays basketball and is a Stephen Curry fan.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. Recently returned to regular gym routine. Plays basketball recreationally with his son. Has dogs at home. Volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle with significant swelling on lateral side. Exquisite tenderness over lateral malleolus. Tenderness noted over medial deltoid region. Skin intact. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Patient able to stand but reports pain with weight-bearing and sensation of instability when walking.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right lateral malleolar fracture, Weber C, displaced and unstable.

Plan:
- Surgical intervention with plate and screw fixation
- Provide crutches
- Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management
- Ice and elevation of ankle; elevation feasible given work-from-home status
- Activity restriction for approximately 3 months
- Clear to continue coaching starting in April
- Follow-up to resume exercise regimen within three-month recovery period
